setup: Stand tall, a dumbbell in each hand
Dumbbells resting in front of your thighs
execution: Raise the dumbbells forward to shoulder height
Keep the slight bend in your elbows
faults: Don't swing with your hips or back
Don't go too heavy; light weights work

notes: Keep the weight light. The front of the shoulder is small, and swinging moves the work elsewhere.
Both arms together, one at a time, or one dumbbell held in both hands are all common. Log the weight of one dumbbell either way.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: One-arm-at-a-time front raise
regressions.reason: Raising one arm while the other rests makes it easier to keep the body still.

progressions.name: Cable front raise
progressions.reason: Keeps tension on through the whole range.

substitutions.name: Lateral raise
substitutions.reason: Same raise out to the sides; more side delts.

substitutions.name: Overhead press
substitutions.reason: Compound press that trains the front delts heavily.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
substitutions.reason: Pressing with dumbbells; front delts and triceps.

substitutions.name: Machine shoulder press
substitutions.reason: Front-delt pressing on a fixed path.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at shoulder height, figure facing right, both dumbbells moving together (the far arm hidden behind the near one).

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, dumbbells in front of the thighs, palms facing the body, elbows softly bent.

keyPositions.label: Up
keyPositions.describe: Arms raised forward to shoulder height, roughly parallel to the floor, elbows still softly bent. Torso upright; no backward lean.

ikHints: Feet and torso fixed; only the arms move
emphasise: Arms rise to shoulder height and no higher
doNotShow: Leaning back to swing the weights
